key_insight: A human–AI discovery loop produced a five-parameter Generalized Boyd construction that avoids degree-skipping while finding irreducible integer polynomials with Mahler measure below 1.255434.
engineering_relevance: The work demonstrates how AI-guided prototyping, distributed numerical search, and exact symbolic verification can jointly advance computational mathematics.
method: Prototype numerical and symbolic solvers through human–AI interaction.
Run parallel searches across distributed clusters.
Extract mathematical hypotheses and verify constructions exactly.
evidence_signal: Across all even degrees up to 2000, the approach improves six previously published values and holds 99.6% of best-known records, with a verified polynomial dataset released.
watch_item: These record-setting constructions do not resolve Lehmer’s problem; numerical candidates still require exact irreducibility and measure verification.
paper_title: Breaking the high-degree barrier in Lehmer's problem with a human-AI discovery loop
